name: Pharaoh
description: Pharaoh living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness

points: Come now therefore, and I will send thee unto Pharaoh, that thou mayest bring forth my people the children of Israel out of Egypt. God rose up a prophet: Moses is the prophet God raised up to deliver us out of ancient Egypt.

note.label: Passover Class: Exodus From America Modern Day Egypt

points: Come now therefore, and I will send thee unto Pharaoh, that thou mayest bring forth my people the children of Israel out of Egypt.

note.label: Exodus 3: The Angel in the Burning Bush

points: Moses said unto God, Who am I, that I should go unto Pharaoh? This shows the humility of the forefathers: none of them sought the position they were given. The Lord chose Moses because He saw the spirit that was in him.

note.label: Exodus 3: The Angel in the Burning Bush

points: Moses took his wife and his sons and returned to the land of Egypt, and Moses took the rod of God in his hand. The LORD told him, Do all those wonders before Pharaoh which I have put in thine hand: but I will harden his heart, that he shall not let the people go.

note.label: Exodus 4: The Three Signs and the Covenant of Circumcision

points: This went to the Pharaoh of Egypt, but the Pharaoh of today is the so-called white man here in Babylon the Great, known as America.

note.label: You Are Hated And In Hell

points: Thou shalt say unto Pharaoh, Thus saith the LORD, Israel is my son, even my firstborn. Israel was not the first nation created; it was among the last. But Israel is the first nation the Most High chose, the apple of His eye from Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob down. If thou refuse to let him go, behold, I will slay thy son, even thy firstborn.

note.label: Exodus 4: The Three Signs and the Covenant of Circumcision

points: Moses and Aaron went in and told Pharaoh, Thus saith the LORD God of Israel, Let my people go, that they may hold a feast unto me in the wilderness. That feast was the Passover.

note.label: Exodus 5: Let My People Go

points: Pharaoh said, Who is the LORD, that I should obey his voice to let Israel go? I know not the LORD, neither will I let Israel go. The Lord had already said He would harden Pharaoh's heart.

note.label: Exodus 5: Let My People Go

points: The officers of the children of Israel, which Pharaoh's taskmasters had set over them, were beaten. Israelites were set as officers over their own people, so that the anger of the oppressed lands on their own brother, the supervisor they can see, instead of on the power above him; it has always been an agenda, and it is the same one today.

note.label: Exodus 5: Let My People Go

points: They met Moses and Aaron and said, The LORD look upon you, and judge; because ye have made our savour to be abhorred in the eyes of Pharaoh, and in the eyes of his servants, to put a sword in their hand to slay us.

note.label: Exodus 5: Let My People Go

points: The Lord renews His promise: Pharaoh will not merely let Israel go, but with a strong hand he shall drive them out of his land.

note.label: Exodus 6: The Promise Renewed and the Generations of Moses and Aaron

points: Moses answered, Behold, the children of Israel have not hearkened unto me; how then shall Pharaoh hear me, who am of uncircumcised lips? This is why Aaron was given him for a mouthpiece in the next chapter.

note.label: Exodus 6: The Promise Renewed and the Generations of Moses and Aaron

points: A former slave became a god to Pharaoh. Imagine what was in Moses' mind when he realised what he had been made.

note.label: The Mind of Mattathias: Let's Search the Scriptures

points: The Lord made Moses a god to Pharaoh, and Aaron his brother was his prophet. Moses was as God and Aaron was the mouthpiece, because Moses kept saying he was of uncircumcised lips.

note.label: Exodus 7: Aaron's Rod and the River Turned to Blood

points: It was Aaron who cast down the rod before Pharaoh, and it became a serpent. A lot of people to this day say it was Moses with the rod, because they do not read the Bible; Moses was telling Aaron what to do, and it was Aaron's rod that turned into the serpent.

note.label: Exodus 7: Aaron's Rod and the River Turned to Blood

points: So Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron and said, Entreat the Lord that he may take away the frogs. Why did Pharaoh not call on Heqet, the god of frogs? He had to go to the Lord.

note.label: Exodus 8: Frogs, Lice, and Swarms of Flies

points: Moses warned Pharaoh, Let not Pharaoh deal deceitfully any more. The Lord removed the swarms so that there remained not one; and Pharaoh hardened his heart at this time also, and would not let the people go.

note.label: Exodus 8: Frogs, Lice, and Swarms of Flies

points: The Lord severed between the cattle of Israel and the cattle of Egypt: all the cattle of Egypt died, but of the cattle of the children of Israel died not one. Pharaoh sent, and behold, there was not one of the cattle of the Israelites dead; and his heart was hardened.

note.label: Exodus 9: Murrain, Boils, and Hail; Goshen Set Apart

points: He that feared the word of the Lord among the servants of Pharaoh made his servants and his cattle flee into the houses; they began to recognize the God of heaven and earth, the God of the Israelites.

note.label: Exodus 9: Murrain, Boils, and Hail; Goshen Set Apart

points: Pharaoh said, I have sinned this time: the Lord is righteous, and I and my people are wicked. This time? So all the other times, none of that was sin? Only now, under the thunder and hail, does he see it.

note.label: Exodus 9: Murrain, Boils, and Hail; Goshen Set Apart

points: When Pharaoh saw that the rain and the hail and the thunders were ceased, he sinned yet more and hardened his heart, he and his servants. He still had the wheat and the rie in the ground, because they were not grown up yet, and that is part of why he went right back to hardening himself.

note.label: Exodus 9: Murrain, Boils, and Hail; Goshen Set Apart

points: The Most High hardened the heart of Pharaoh and of his servants so that he might show his signs and exemplify his power in the earth. After he brought down Egypt and delivered the people, every nation feared Israel and the God of Israel.

The scripture said to Pharaoh, Even for this same purpose have I raised thee up, that I might show my power in thee, and that my name might be declared throughout all the earth. He has mercy on whom he will have mercy, and whom he will he hardeneth.

note.label: Exodus 10: The Most High Hardens Pharaoh to Shew His Signs

points: Moses went in to Pharaoh with a staff and an ultimatum: how long wilt thou refuse to humble thyself? Let my people go, or tomorrow, in twenty four hours, the locusts come into thy coast.

note.label: Exodus 10: The Most High Hardens Pharaoh to Shew His Signs

points: The locusts would cover the face of the earth so no one could see the ground, eat the residue that escaped the hail, and fill the houses of Pharaoh, of his servants, and of all the Egyptians, such as neither their fathers nor their fathers' fathers had seen.

note.label: Exodus 10: The Most High Hardens Pharaoh to Shew His Signs

points: Pharaoh's own servants pleaded with him: how long shall this man be a snare unto us? Knowest thou not yet that Egypt is destroyed?

note.label: Exodus 10: The Most High Hardens Pharaoh to Shew His Signs

points: Pharaoh offered to let only the men go, and Moses and Aaron were driven out from his presence.

note.label: Exodus 10: The Most High Hardens Pharaoh to Shew His Signs

points: When the judgment got real, Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron in haste and confessed, I have sinned against the Lord your God and against you. Everything had been eaten by the locusts, and now he begged that this death only be taken from him.

note.label: Exodus 10: The Most High Hardens Pharaoh to Shew His Signs

points: But the Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart, so that he would not let the children of Israel go. The Most High is in ultimate control even of the devil; he is the omnipotent master of all existence, and nothing can be done outside his will.

note.label: Exodus 10: The Most High Hardens Pharaoh to Shew His Signs

points: After three days of darkness Pharaoh called for Moses: go, serve the Lord, only let your flocks and your herds be stayed. Go, but leave all your possessions in Egypt.

note.label: Exodus 10: The Most High Hardens Pharaoh to Shew His Signs

points: The Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart yet again, and Pharaoh threatened Moses: see my face no more, for in that day thou seest my face thou shalt die. After the rivers turned to blood, the hail with flaming fire, the locusts, and the darkness, Pharaoh still thought he was in a position to give out threats. That is the deceivableness of the strong delusion: God sends it so that they should believe a lie.

note.label: Exodus 10: The Most High Hardens Pharaoh to Shew His Signs

points: Yet will I bring one plague more upon Pharaoh, and upon Egypt. Them wonders that were brought upon Pharaoh and Egypt are called plagues.

note.label: The Plagues Coming to America

points: Hear how Moses spoke to Pharaoh. Yet will I bring one plague more upon Pharaoh and upon Egypt; afterwards he will let you go, and he shall surely thrust you out altogether. The other times the Lord hardened his heart because he wanted to show his wonderful power. Let every man borrow of his neighbour jewels of silver and gold; the Lord gave the people favour in the sight of the Egyptians, and the man Moses was very great in the land. Remember Moses at first was dismayed: who made thee a ruler over us; he had to run when he tried to step up and defend his people. Now he came back as a hero for his people, empowered by the one true God.

note.label: Making Our Face Harder Than Their Face

points: The Most High already knew what was going down: yet will I bring one plague more upon Pharaoh and upon Egypt. This last plague would end it, and when Pharaoh let the people go he would thrust them out hence altogether, with the quickness.

note.label: Exodus 11: The Death of the Firstborn Announced

points: Moses was very great in the land of Egypt, in the sight of Pharaoh's servants and in the sight of the people; he had a good report. Israel in spiritual Egypt must deal the same way: have the respect of the people, and if people despise you, let it be because they hate God and the word you teach, not because you are in wickedness, shady dealings, deceit, or disrespect.

note.label: Exodus 11: The Death of the Firstborn Announced

points: About midnight will I go out into the midst of Egypt: and all the firstborn in the land of Egypt shall die, from the firstborn of Pharaoh that sitteth upon his throne, even unto the firstborn of the maidservant that is behind the mill; and there shall be a great cry throughout all the land of Egypt. That is another plague. Now let us take that plague to America.

note.label: The Plagues Coming to America

points: About midnight the Lord would go out into the midst of Egypt, and all the firstborn in the land would die, from the firstborn of Pharaoh on his throne to the firstborn of the maidservant behind the mill, and all the firstborn of beasts.

note.label: Exodus 11: The Death of the Firstborn Announced

points: All these thy servants shall come down unto me and bow down, saying, get thee out, and all the people that follow thee. And he went out from Pharaoh in a great anger. Moses had to drop the mic: this is going to be it, Pharaoh; I warned you about the frogs and the blood and you would not listen. See the boldness of a servant of the Lord. And the Lord said, Pharaoh shall not hearken unto you: he is going to be hardened, but do not stop doing what you are doing, that my wonders may be multiplied. This is why some of the wicked have to go; do not feel sorry for them. Go in and do your mission, teach, prophesy, edify, build up, but the Lord has to show the wicked of our people: all you had to do was repent; multiple times he reached out through the mouth of the prophets and they refused. He is doing the same thing with America, hardening their hearts; they do not see the stress of the people and do not care about black and Hispanic America; those they cannot use and manipulate they want to eliminate. But there is a God, and he has a mission for us. Do not be afraid of it.

note.label: Making Our Face Harder Than Their Face

points: All Pharaoh's servants would come down and bow to Moses, saying, Get thee out, and all the people that follow thee; and Moses went out from Pharaoh in a great anger.

note.label: Exodus 11: The Death of the Firstborn Announced

points: Pharaoh would not hearken, that the wonders of the Most High might be multiplied in the land of Egypt. He is in control of the leaders of every country, presidents, governors, senators, congressmen, and mayors alike; whoever gets in the seat, he twists and turns them about like the river.

note.label: Exodus 11: The Death of the Firstborn Announced

points: At midnight the Lord smote all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh that sat on his throne unto the firstborn of the captive in the dungeon, and all the firstborn of cattle. Even the prisoners' firstborn died, and Pharaoh's own son died.

note.label: Exodus 12: The Lord's Passover

points: Pharaoh rose up in the night, he and all his servants and all the Egyptians, and there was a great cry in Egypt, for there was not a house where there was not one dead.

note.label: Exodus 12: The Lord's Passover

points: When Pharaoh let the people go, God led them not through the way of the land of the Philistines, although that was near, lest peradventure the people repent when they see war and return to Egypt. Israel would have been fearful at the sight of the Philistine army and turned back.

note.label: Exodus 13: By Strength of Hand the Lord Brought Us Out

points: The heart of Pharaoh and of his servants turned as soon as the people were gone: why have we done this, that we have let Israel go from serving us? The oppressor does not release his slaves gladly.

note.label: Exodus 14: The Salvation of the Lord at the Red Sea

points: The Lord hardened the heart of Pharaoh, and he pursued after the children of Israel. Even after the Lord killed all the firstborn in Egypt, Pharaoh still went after the Israelites; but the Lord made him do that.

note.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

points: I will get me honour upon Pharaoh, and upon all his host. The Lord wanted honor. He said: I am going to harden the Egyptians' hearts to make them chase after you into the sea, so the whole world could talk about what I did to the Egyptians. Even to this day they are talking about what was done to the Egyptians. And the Egyptians shall know that I am the Lord.

note.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

points: Pharaoh's chariots and his chosen captains are drowned in the Red Sea. Their oppressors were killed in front of them.

note.label: The Slave Mentality Yesterday & Today: the True Diaspora

points: Pharaoh's chariots and his host hath he cast into the sea: his chosen captains also are drowned in the Red Sea. Who did that? The Lord. Thy right hand, O Lord, hath dashed in pieces the enemy. This is the wars of the Lord we are reading about: when the Lord fought against the Egyptians, drowned them in the Red Sea, and brought plagues upon them.

note.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

points: Then thou shalt say unto thy son, we were Pharaoh's bondmen in Egypt, and the Lord brought us out with a mighty hand, and shewed signs and wonders upon Egypt and upon Pharaoh; he brought us out that he might bring us in, to give us the land which he sware unto our fathers. The Most High always keeps his covenant; he is not a man, that he should lie.

note.label: Deuteronomy 6: Teach Them Diligently unto Thy Children

points: He kept the oath sworn unto the fathers and redeemed Israel out of the house of bondmen, from the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt; Israel came out from under Rameses.

note.label: Deuteronomy 7: A Holy People, Chosen Above All People

points: Their own priests warned them from Israel's history: wherefore then do ye harden your hearts, as the Egyptians and Pharaoh hardened their hearts? They did not want to end up like Egypt, so they said, let us learn the lesson and get this ark back.

note.label: 1 Samuel 6: The Ark Returned with a Trespass Offering

points: For the scripture saith unto Pharaoh, Even for this same purpose have I raised thee up. So this is being said about Esau. For the scripture saith unto Pharaoh — for means because. Listen good. The statement is being pushed to Esau to tell him, listen, the reason why you are raised up is because the same thing happened to Pharaoh. The reason why the Lord is going to judge you is because he did the same thing to Pharaoh. The same reason why you have got the power that you have got now is because he did the same thing to Pharaoh.

That I might shew my power in thee. That I might show my power when I destroy you as the vessels of my wrath, like I destroyed ancient Pharaoh. And that my name might be declared throughout all the earth. But when the Lord destroys Esau, his name is going to be declared all over the earth the same way that it was when he destroyed ancient Pharaoh.

note.label: The Exponential Maturation In The Days Of Decadence

points: For the same purpose have I raised thee up, that I might show my power in thee: as Pharaoh was raised up to be a god on earth so the God of the Hebrews could be declared in Egypt's fall, so Esau is raised up with his nuclear weapons.

note.label: Woe to Amerikkka

points: For this same purpose have I raised thee up: Paul could not condemn Rome aloud so he compared Esau to Pharaoh. God raised Pharaoh, Rome and now America, the extension of Rome, to show his power; no other nation takes America down, so he lets her have every advance and then flexes.

note.label: Zionism in the Face of Syria & Hezbollah
